 The AMD Developer Hackathon: ACT III is a hands-on event for developers, founders, engineers and builders who want to push what’s possible with AI on real infrastructure. Whether you are just starting out or already shipping, you can jump in and start creating.
 You’ll be working with AMD GPUs in the Cloud with the ROCm software stack, AMD's open-source GPU computing platform. Everything runs fully in the cloud, so there is no local hardware to set up and you can focus on building instead of configuration.
 One hackathon. Three cities. One special weekend in Italy.
 This edition of the AMD Developer Hackathon comes with a special on-site experience across three locations in Italy: Rome, Milan, and Imperia .
 The hackathon remains open online throughout the event, while selected participants can also join us in person for the on-site phase. If approved, you’ll choose one of the three locations 
 to build alongside other developers, get hands-on support, and showcase your project live.

 Challenges 
 Solve a real Business Problem with AMD technology
 Choose one of four business challenges and build a working product on AMD infrastructure. We are looking for projects that solve a real problem for a real user. Your idea can use language models, computer vision, audio, agents, predictive models, or a combination of technologies.
 The important part is simple: the product should work, and AMD technology should power a meaningful part of it.
 Build the next generation of AI agents and high-performance apps — powered by AMD
 This hackathon is your space to explore, experiment and create with AMD GPUs in the cloud and the ROCm software stack. No hardware, no complex setup — just access to powerful compute and the freedom to build what you actually care about.
 Whether you want to prototype an idea, push a system to its limits or try something completely new, this is the place to do it. Build an application, agent or developer tool that feels real, works end to end, and shows what AMD’s compute stack can unlock.

 Choose Your track
 Track 1 by partner: Vibe Generation 
 Intelligent Industry
 Help factories spot problems earlier and operate better.
 Read the full brief Hide the brief 
 Factories produce data from machines, cameras, sensors, maintenance reports, and technical manuals. The problem is rarely a lack of information. The problem is knowing what matters and what to do next.
 Build a product that helps a manufacturer reduce downtime, improve quality, increase safety, or use resources more efficiently.
 Ideas
 Predict equipment failures
 Detect defects from images or video
 Explain production anomalies
 Help technicians search manuals and maintenance records
 Recommend maintenance actions
 Monitor safety conditions
 Reduce energy or material waste
 Your demo
 Show your product processing realistic industrial data and producing a useful alert, explanation, recommendation, or action. Make it clear who would use the product and what result it improves.
 Good projects will show
 A real manufacturing problem
 A working product, not only a dashboard or presentation
 Results that operators can understand
 A measurable improvement in time, cost, safety, quality, or efficiency
 Track 2 by partner: Vibe Generation 
 Health and Wellbeing
 Make a part of the patient journey safer, clearer, or easier.
 Read the full brief Hide the brief 
 Patients and healthcare workers deal with long documents, scattered information, repetitive administration, language barriers, and limited time.
 Build a product that helps patients, caregivers, or healthcare staff handle one part of this journey better.
 Ideas
 Patient intake
 Medical record summaries
 Appointment preparation
 Care navigation
 Clearer discharge instructions
 Multilingual patient communication
 Healthcare document processing
 Administrative workflow automation
 Wellbeing and prevention support
 Your demo
 Show a realistic case from the first input to the final result. Your product should make uncertainty visible. It should also know when a person needs to review or take over the case.
 Safety rules
 The product must not present autonomous diagnosis or treatment as medical advice. Explain how you handle:
 Incorrect or unsupported responses
 Sensitive information
 Uncertain results
 High risk decisions
 Human review
 Good projects will show
 A clearly defined patient or staff need
 Responsible handling of health information
 Useful and understandable results
 A measurable improvement in time, accuracy, accessibility, or workload
 Track 3 by partner: Vibe Generation 
 Reinvent Commerce
 Help a business understand its customers and take better action.
 Read the full brief Hide the brief 
 Retailers have product data, transactions, inventory, reviews, support conversations, and marketing results. These sources are often disconnected, which makes it difficult to turn them into useful decisions.
 Build a product that helps a business attract, serve, convert, or retain customers.
 Ideas
 Shopping assistants
 Product discovery and recommendations
 Customer support
 Demand and inventory planning
 Product catalogue enrichment
 Review and sentiment analysis
 Promotion planning
 Churn prevention
 Accessible and multilingual shopping
 In store computer vision
 Your demo
 Show how your product turns customer or business data into a useful recommendation or action.
 If your product predicts demand, sales, or customer behaviour, explain how the prediction was calculated. Do not use a language model as the only forecasting method.
 Good projects will show
 A real customer or merchant problem
 A useful commercial action
 Relevant recommendations or personalization
 A measurable effect on revenue, margin, conversion, retention, inventory, or service quality
 Track 4 by partner: Vibe Generation 
 Create a New Kind of Experience
 Build a media, marketing, or entertainment experience that was not practical before generative AI.
 Read the full brief Hide the brief 
 Do more than generate an image, advertisement, or chatbot. Create something that responds to its audience, changes with context, or produces a different experience for each person.
 Ideas
 Personalized video
 Interactive stories
 Audience driven entertainment
 Adaptive campaigns
 Multilingual creative content
 Generative brand experiences
 Responsive sound or visual environments
 New social media formats
 Accessible media experiences
 Creative quality control
 Your demo
 Show the experience changing for at least two different audiences, situations, or inputs. 
Explain:
 What the team created
 What the models generated or decided
 How you controlled quality and consistency
 How much each generated experience costs
 Who would pay for it and why
 Good projects will show
 An original concept
 A strong user experience
 A thoughtful combination of human creativity and technology
 A product that could work at a realistic cost
 Technology requirement: build on AMD
 Every project must run a meaningful part of its workload on AMD infrastructure or AMD hardware. Teams may use:
 AMD Developer Cloud
 AMD Instinct accelerators
 AMD ROCm
 AMD Ryzen AI
 AMD Radeon hardware
 Other approved AMD powered infrastructure provided during the event
 The AMD component must be part of the working product shown to the judges. Teams may choose their own compatible models, frameworks, and development tools.
 Partner awards
 Google and Evolus technologies are optional. Teams that use an eligible partner technology can also compete for that partner’s prize. A single project may qualify for the main challenge prize, one partner prize, or both partner prizes.

 Track by partner: Evolus 
 Evolus Business Agents on AMD
 Build an AI agent that runs a real business process end to end, on Evolus, powered by an open model served on AMD.
 Pick a process that a real company runs every day and let an agent run it. The agent takes the input (an email, a PDF, a recording, a web form, a chat), reasons over it with an open model running on AMD, and acts: it runs an Evolus workflow, turns documents into data, uses AI Tools, updates another system, or hands the case to a person when it should.
 Requirements
 Build in a free Evolus event workspace , created at app.evolus.ai with the event code shared at kickoff.
 Bring your own model: the main agent must use an open model served on AMD infrastructure through your own vLLM endpoint on AMD Developer Cloud.
 Use at least two Evolus building blocks: workflows, document extractors, AI Tools, knowledge libraries, MCP connectors, sub-agents, chat widget.
 Drive Evolus from your app through its APIs: the Evolus REST API for workflows, extractors, AI Tools and libraries; agent chat through the REST API or the OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
 Follow the hackathon submission rules: containerized app, public GitHub repository, a README that runs. Never commit API keys: use environment variables.
 Sample use cases
 Use case 
 Input 
 What the solution does 
 Invoice and order intake 
 Emails with PDF attachments 
 A workflow started by incoming email reads the PDF, extracts the fields into JSON, matches them to the order and flags mismatches to a person 
 Support desk on company knowledge 
 Chat, email or website widget 
 An agent answers from the company’s documents with sources and passes the case to a person when unsure 
 Lead qualification 
 Chat widget on a website 
 Qualifies the visitor, books a call and pushes the lead to a CRM through MCP 
 Contract review 
 Uploaded contracts 
 Extracts key clauses, compares them with the company’s standard terms and redacts personal data before sharing 
 Multilingual documents 
 PDF and Word files 
 Translates manuals and offers keeping their layout, then files them through a workflow 
 Meeting follow-up 
 Recordings of calls and meetings 
 Turns the recording into minutes and action items and sends them to the attendees 
 Judging
 The hackathon’s four criteria, read on this track:
 Application of Technology
 How deeply the solution uses Evolus building blocks, and how well the AMD-hosted model is integrated.
 Business Value
 A real process, a clear user, a measurable gain.
 Originality
 A new approach, or a process nobody automated this way.
 Presentation
 A clear demo and pitch.
 To verify the requirements, the Evolus team reviews the configuration and usage statistics of each event workspace: the connected model endpoint, the building blocks used and the API calls.
 More tracks — to be announced
 Further tracks, task details and sample use cases will be published here before the kickoff.

 Partners 
 Build on AMD GPUs in the cloud
 Lead partner
 This hackathon gives developers the opportunity to explore and build AI workloads using AMD’s cloud-based AI stack. All development happens on cloud-accessible AMD GPUs, so there is no need to own or manage hardware.
 The focus is on experimenting, benchmarking and running real workloads in a flexible environment. During the hackathon, teams can choose to work with the technologies below.
 AMD Developer Cloud
 On-demand access to AMD GPUs through the cloud. Spin up a GPU environment in minutes and build and test AI workloads without infrastructure overhead.
 Training and fine-tuning models
 Benchmarking AI workloads on AMD GPUs
 Prototyping before moving to on-prem infrastructure
 ROCm
 ROCm is AMD’s open-source software platform for GPU computing — the AMD equivalent of CUDA. It runs AI/ML and HPC workloads on AMD GPUs.
 Running PyTorch and TensorFlow on AMD GPUs
 Porting CUDA-based workloads to AMD hardware
 High-performance AI and ML workloads

 Vibe Generation
 Vibe Generation is the project founded by Paolo Bonetti to integrate specialized professionals and artificial intelligence tools into the real-world processes of businesses.
The model was created to support companies, brands and organizations in moving from the occasional use of AI tools to building hybrid teams and processes, in which technology and human skills work together.
The project focuses in particular on the relationship between artificial intelligence, talent, judgment and organizational transformation.
 Evolus AI
 The platform to build AI agents that run real business processes. Bring your own AMD-hosted model and ship an agent that does real work.
 Evolus gives companies AI agents that read documents, answer from company knowledge, run automations and act on the systems they already use through APIs and MCP. Businesses also use Evolus for digital employees that work in email and Microsoft Teams, and for an AI Switchboard that answers the phone.
 For developers, everything is driven by the Evolus REST API, agents can also be reached through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and an MCP server lets coding agents build on Evolus directly. During the hackathon every team brings its own model.

 Technology 
 Technology & access
 Teams connect their own model and build around it: agents, business automations, document extractors, knowledge libraries and ready-made AI Tools, all driven by API.
 Agents and sub-agents
 Agents with tools and memory, running on the team’s own model.
 Evolus REST API ( ask , streaming ask-stream ); for chat also the OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions 
 Workflows (business automations)
 Multi-step pipelines of agents, document reading, extractors and webhooks, with branches, loops and parallel steps. They start from an API call, an incoming email or a schedule: files in, result out to a callback URL.
 Evolus REST API: POST /api/v1/workflows/{id}/execute with text and files, then the execution status
 Document extractors
 Turn PDFs, scans and images into structured JSON, following a schema you define.
 Evolus REST API, or as a workflow step
 AI Tools
 Eleven ready-made tools: document to structured data (JSON, CSV, XML), table extraction, translation of PDF and Word files keeping the original layout, real redaction of personal data in PDFs, summaries, meeting minutes from audio or video, email writing and replies, rewriting, plain-language simplification, sentiment, comparison of two texts.
 Evolus REST API: /api/v1/ai-tools/{tool}/run , run-media for audio and video, run-file for file in, file out
 Knowledge libraries (RAG)
 Upload documents or import web pages; agents answer from them, with sources.
 Evolus REST API, attached to agents
 Webhooks
 Notify your own systems when something happens.
 Evolus REST API
 MCP connectors
 Connect agents to external systems through MCP servers, including your own.
 Configured in the workspace
 Chat widget
 Put an agent on any website.
 One script tag
 Evolus MCP server
 Build and manage agents, workflows and libraries from Claude Code, Cursor or any MCP client.
 https://api.evolus.ai/mcp 
 Evolus Studio
 A coding agent for terminal and desktop, built on the open-source OpenCode, with the Evolus MCP tools built in.
 Desktop app and CLI
 Bring your own model. Event workspaces run their agents on the model each team connects: an open model through a vLLM endpoint on AMD Developer Cloud, or any OpenAI-compatible provider.
 Which API for what. Workflows, extractors, AI Tools and knowledge libraries use the Evolus REST API; only agent chat is also available through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Document reading, AI Tools and knowledge indexing run on Evolus and use the workspace credits.
 Access, free for every participant
 Go to app.evolus.ai and sign in with GitHub, Google, Apple or Microsoft.
 Enter the event code, shared at kickoff: a free workspace until October 31, 2026, for up to 6 team members, with 50,000 platform credits and no credit card.
 Connect your model, create an API key and start building.
 Evolus Studio: download link shared before the kickoff; sign in with your Evolus account.
